_comment: Guided tour for the FPS JSON editor card. Steps point at real controls; the ones with an await wait until the user presses the control.

steps.title: What this editor is for
steps.text:
An fps.json file says where dyes sit on a structure (positions) and which FRET distances were measured between them (distances). The docking and screening tools read it.

You can open an existing file with Load, or build one here from nothing. Ten steps; you press the buttons, the tour only points at them.

steps.title: Add a position
steps.text: A position is one labelling site. Press Add Row to start one.

steps.title: Choose the structure
steps.text:
Press Fetch PDB... and type a 4-character PDB ID (for example 1R0A): the structure is downloaded from the RCSB for the selected row and shown in the 3D View. Browse PDB... takes a file instead; typing an ID or a path into PDB file or ID does the same.

The chain, residue and atom lists in Selected position are filled from it, and the row is named from its chain and residue (for example A132).

steps.title: Walk the dye along the chain
steps.text: Residue ▶ and ◀ Residue move the selected position one residue on; its accessible volume is recomputed and the 3D View shows where the dye can now be. The selected position's volume stands out, the others are muted.

steps.title: Place it in 3D
steps.text: In the 3D View, click an atom: the selected position is attached there (with no position selected, a click starts a new one). Click a coloured sphere (an AV's mean position) to select that position. Drag to rotate, wheel to zoom. Any view's tab can be dragged to rearrange the window.

steps.title: Compute the accessible volumes
steps.text: The accessible volume is where the dye can be, given its linker. It is computed for every position that has a structure, chain, residue and atom; Compute AVs recomputes them all.

steps.title: Distances between positions
steps.text: Open the Distances tab: a restraint joins two positions.

steps.title: Add a restraint
steps.text: Add Row adds an empty restraint; choose its two labels and the numbers in Selected restraint. It is named label1_label2.

steps.title: The raw file
steps.text: The JSON tab shows exactly what will be written. You can edit it by hand; Update in the toolbar reads your text back into the tables.

steps.title: Save it
steps.text: Save writes the fps.json. Press Help for the file format and what each tab does.
